The primary purpose of Loopalyzer is to visualise how the Loop closed loop system performs. It may work with other setups as well, both closed and open loop, and non loop. However depending on which uploader you use, how frequent it is able to capture your data and upload, and how it is able to backfill missing data some graphs may have gaps or even be completely empty. Always ensure the graphs look reasonable. Best is to view one day at a time and scroll through a number of days first to see.

Loopalyzer includes a time shift feature. If you for example have breakfast at 07:00 one day and at 08:00 the day after your average blood glucose curve these two days will most likely look flattened and not show the actual response after a breakfast. Time shift will compute the average time these meals were eaten and then shift all data (carbs, insulin, basal etc.) during both days the corresponding time difference so that both meals align with the average meal start time.

In this example all data from first day is pushed 30 minutes forward in time and all data from second day 30 minutes backward in time so it appears as if you had had breakfast at 07:30 both days. This allows you to see your actual average blood glucose response from a meal.

Time shift highlights the period after the average meal start time in gray, for the duration of the DIA (Duration of Insulin Action). As all data points the entire day are shifted the curves outside the gray area may not be accurate.
Note that time shift is available only when viewing multiple days.

rows.key: The primary purpose of Loopalyzer is to visualise how the Loop closed loop system performs. It may work with other setups as well, both closed and open loop, and non loop. However depending on which uploader you use, how frequent it is able to capture your data and upload, and how it is able to backfill missing data some graphs may have gaps or even be completely empty. Always ensure the graphs look reasonable. Best is to view one day at a time and scroll through a number of days first to see.
rows.original: The primary purpose of Loopalyzer is to visualise how the Loop closed loop system performs. It may work with other setups as well, both closed and open loop, and non loop. However depending on which uploader you use, how frequent it is able to capture your data and upload, and how it is able to backfill missing data some graphs may have gaps or even be completely empty. Always ensure the graphs look reasonable. Best is to view one day at a time and scroll through a number of days first to see.
rows.replacement: ループ分析は、Loopの自動制御システムがどのように動作しているかを可視化するための機能です。他の自動制御、手動制御、ループを使わない構成でも動作する場合があります。ただし、送信機器の種類、データ取得と送信の頻度、欠損データを補完できるかによって、グラフに空白ができたり全体が空になったりすることがあります。グラフが妥当な表示になっているか、必ず確認してください。まず1日ずつ表示し、複数の日を順に確認する方法が適しています。

rows.key: Loopalyzer includes a time shift feature. If you for example have breakfast at 07:00 one day and at 08:00 the day after your average blood glucose curve these two days will most likely look flattened and not show the actual response after a breakfast. Time shift will compute the average time these meals were eaten and then shift all data (carbs, insulin, basal etc.) during both days the corresponding time difference so that both meals align with the average meal start time.
rows.original: Loopalyzer includes a time shift feature. If you for example have breakfast at 07:00 one day and at 08:00 the day after your average blood glucose curve these two days will most likely look flattened and not show the actual response after a breakfast. Time shift will compute the average time these meals were eaten and then shift all data (carbs, insulin, basal etc.) during both days the corresponding time difference so that both meals align with the average meal start time.
rows.replacement: ループ分析には食事の時刻をそろえる機能があります。たとえば、ある日の朝食が7時、翌日の朝食が8時だった場合、2日間の平均血糖曲線は平坦になり、朝食後の実際の反応が見えにくくなります。この機能は食事開始の平均時刻を求め、両日のすべてのデータ（糖質、インスリン、基礎インスリンなど）を時刻差の分だけ移動して、食事の開始時刻を平均にそろえます。

rows.key: In this example all data from first day is pushed 30 minutes forward in time and all data from second day 30 minutes backward in time so it appears as if you had had breakfast at 07:30 both days. This allows you to see your actual average blood glucose response from a meal.
rows.original: In this example all data from first day is pushed 30 minutes forward in time and all data from second day 30 minutes backward in time so it appears as if you had had breakfast at 07:30 both days. This allows you to see your actual average blood glucose response from a meal.
rows.replacement: この例では、1日目の全データを30分後へ、2日目の全データを30分前へ移動し、両日とも7時30分に朝食を取ったように表示します。これにより、食事に対する実際の平均血糖反応を確認できます。

rows.key: Time shift highlights the period after the average meal start time in gray, for the duration of the DIA (Duration of Insulin Action). As all data points the entire day are shifted the curves outside the gray area may not be accurate.
rows.original: Time shift highlights the period after the average meal start time in gray, for the duration of the DIA (Duration of Insulin Action). As all data points the entire day are shifted the curves outside the gray area may not be accurate.
rows.replacement: 時刻をそろえた表示では、平均食事開始時刻からインスリン作用時間（DIA）が経過するまでの区間を灰色で示します。1日分すべてのデータを移動するため、灰色の区間以外の曲線は正確でない場合があります。

rows.key: Note that time shift is available only when viewing multiple days.
rows.original: Note that time shift is available only when viewing multiple days.
rows.replacement: 食事の時刻をそろえる機能は、複数日を表示する場合だけ使用できます。
